title: Control Plane catalog package object
description: One wrapper for the manifest and every catalog kind: apiVersion + kind + key + spec. spec is the control-plane API request body in camelCase without the identity field. The schema checks the shape; the final check is done by the core (and by package-sdk check with its validators).

version.description: Ontology version in the package, an integer: an inclusion refers to it as name@version, an edit is a new version

envOrUuid.description: UUID or an installation ${VARIABLE} (environment topology is not written into the package)

secretName.description: Secret name on the node; the value is not written into the description

agentSpec.description: Agent: who it is, what work it takes, with what and how it executes, where it is placed. Every change is a new immutable revision in the core; a run remembers its revision.

identity.description: Identity: the core and IAM principal and its binding to permissions, created and maintained by the platform. Permissions are no broader than those of whoever applies the description.

iam.description: IAM part of the account: audiences and the scope ceiling. Data for whoever issues the account (bootstrap, executor node controller); the core stores it but does not interpret it.

scopeCeiling.description: Scope <audience>:<action>, segments may be dotted (control-plane:read, iam:identities.link)

work.description: What work the agent takes from the queue

executor.description: What the agent executes work with. The kind is data (a string for the core); the default image is chosen by the node, an image from the description only from the node's list.

image.description: Executor image: [registry[:port]/]path:tag, …@sha256:<64 hex> or …:tag@sha256:<64 hex>; a tag or digest is required. The node runs it only if the image is in the node's executors.<kind>.images list, otherwise image_not_allowed; without the field, the kind's default image
image.$comment: grammar CP-ADR-0073 З1; amendment TAI-ADR-0052 item 7, TAI-ADR-0062 item 9

instructions.description: Instructions for the executor: a layer after the platform, project and task type instructions

workingCopy.description: Task working copy. Interpreted by the executor daemon, the core stores the object as data; the shape is set by the executor kind: shapes per kind are in agentWorkingCopies: for the code executor kind, one repository or a catalog with a task field, for other kinds, one repository
workingCopy.$comment: TAI-ADR-0016 item 5; TAI-ADR-0063, amendments ADR-0052 item 1 and CP-ADR-0073 items 1, 14

skills.description: Which skills the agent executes itself and where they may connect

audiences.description: IAM audiences the skills get a token for

invoke.description: Skill versions the agent invokes through the core (name@version) rather than executing itself; the registry assigns them to the agent's principal

placement.description: Where and how many: none means identity only, without a process (service account)
placement.$comment: if/then/else rather than oneOf: with oneOf a finding loses the path into the object (spec/placement instead of spec/placement/resources/cpus)

secrets.description: Secrets the node must have: static ones (a file in the node's secrets directory) and issued ones, which the node issues and renews itself, e.g. an hourly forge-token from the forge app installation. Declared the same way, by name; the material is not written into the description

cpus.description: Whole CPUs: the core canonical hash of a revision rejects fractional numbers (non_canonical_value)

drainSeconds.description: How long to wait for the current run before switching to a new revision

connections.description: Keys of the tenant's connections whose access material the agent may read. Whether such a connection exists is not checked on publish; a non-empty list needs connections.manage of whoever applies it

repositoryKey.description: Canonical repository key in the working copy catalog: ASCII, as in the task's customFields. Keys and aliases are matched case-insensitively (casefold): this is how the executor daemon and tasks.check@1 resolve the task key
repositoryKey.$comment: (?![\s\S]) after $ because $ in Python re allows a trailing newline

repositoryAlias.description: Former repository name (map key, repository row of the task document, connector deduplication key): Latin and Cyrillic letters, digits, . _ -. Matched against the task key case-insensitively (casefold)
repositoryAlias.$comment: Letters as explicit ranges (Latin with Latin-1 and Extended-A/B, Cyrillic) rather than \p{L}: Python re, which package-sdk checks with, does not know \p{…}. (?![\s\S]) after $ because $ in Python re allows a trailing newline

workingCopyPath.description: A directory in the working copy relative to its root: one name (flat layout, control-plane) or a path of several segments joined by / (services/control-plane, sdk/platform-auth-sdk). A segment starts with a lowercase Latin letter or a digit, so . and .. do not pass; an absolute path, an empty segment (//, a trailing /) and a backslash are rejected
workingCopyPath.$comment: TAI-ADR-0064 items 1–2. (?![\s\S]) after $ because $ in Python re allows a trailing newline

agentWorkingCopies.description: Shapes of the workingCopy section per executor kind: the core stores the section as data, this schema and the executor daemon check it

single.description: Legacy shape: one repository, neighbours and superproject by address

directory.description: Directory of the repository in the working copy: a name (flat layout) or a path of several segments

neighbours.description: Neighbour repositories at revisions pinned by the superproject. The key is the neighbour's directory in the working copy: a name or a path of several segments

publish.description: Publish the task branch to the forge

checks.description: Run the checks of .agents/runner.yaml of the base revision before hand-in; the report goes to metadata.checks of the commit artifact

review.description: Deprecated: review is declared by the task type as acceptance criteria; the section is removed together with the daemon's auto-review

taskTypes.description: Task types that get a review

catalog.description: Repository catalog: the only source of clone, neighbour and publication addresses. The task repository is a catalog key or an alias in the task field repositoryField; an address from the task is not accepted, there is no default. Keys and aliases are matched case-insensitively (casefold): this is how the executor daemon and tasks.check@1 resolve the task key. package-sdk check verifies that superproject refers to a catalog key and that keys and aliases (casefold), addresses (normalized) and directories are unambiguous across entries

repositoryField.description: Name of the task's customFields field holding the repository key (repositoryKey for coding-task)

superproject.description: Catalog key whose submodules pin the neighbours' revisions

publish.description: Publish the task branch to the forge; a catalog entry may override it

checks.description: Run the checks of .agents/runner.yaml of the base revision before hand-in; the report goes to metadata.checks of the commit artifact

url.description: Clone address: an installation ${VARIABLE} or https without credentials, query and fragment (environment topology is not written into the package). Host: DNS labels, port 1–65535; path segments: ASCII without dot segments or a leading dot, since the mirror name is taken from the last segment. package-sdk check looks for matching addresses of two entries after normalization (no trailing /, no .git, case-insensitive)

baseRef.description: Task base branch, a git ref name: no leading - / ., no spaces or control characters, no .., @{, //, ~^:?*[\ and no trailing / . .lock

directory.description: Directory in the working copy: a name (flat layout) or a path of several segments (services/control-plane). It does not repeat the directory or the key of another entry, and is neither inside the directory of another entry nor contains it — checked by package-sdk check

publish.description: false means a neighbour the agent does not write to; defaults to the catalog's publish

aliases.description: Former names accepted instead of the key; matching is case-insensitive (casefold), so aliases repeat neither their own nor other keys and aliases, even in another case

claude-code.description: One repository (legacy shape) or a catalog: the presence of repositories or repositoryField selects the catalog

agentExecutors.description: Executor kind parameters; the core stores them without interpreting, this schema and the adapter check them

tools.description: Narrowing of the agent's tools; the ban on authoritative Control Plane commands is not lifted

skills.description: Skills-only executor: what to execute is the agent's skills section; params are non-secret skill settings

env.description: Non-secret skill settings (portal address, limits): environment variables of every local skill call on the skills host. No secrets here: names like *TOKEN, *SECRET, *PASSWORD, *API_KEY are forbidden, secrets come as node secret files (placement.secrets); host names (CONTROL_PLANE_*, IAM_*, PATH…) are forbidden too

git-connector.description: Git observation source: what to observe and which observations to produce. The cursor lives in the replica volume, observations go to POST /observations of the agent's workspace.

observe.description: commits — repo.commit_observed; adrRegistry — adr.registry_observed; ciRuns — ci.run_observed

knowledgeSnapshots.description: Send contract snapshots to memory via POST /knowledge/snapshots

registryRepository.description: Repository to read the ADR registry from (a name from repositories)

observer.description: Integration package observation source (connector = observer + skills): a long-lived process that polls an external system in a loop and writes observations to the agent's workspace (POST /observations). What to poll is config, interpreted by the integration code; which code is entrypoint, which the observer kind image on the node must contain. The cursor lives in the replica volume, secrets come only as node secret files (placement.secrets).

entrypoint.description: Integration observer "module:function"; the image process checks that it executes exactly this one

config.description: Integration parameters (filters, addresses, limits) are package data. No secrets here: keys like *token, *secret, *password are forbidden

acceptanceCriterion.description: Acceptance criterion: the core checks the spec grammar per kind

when.description: $.task… paths; the criterion runs only if all are non-empty, otherwise skipped

typeKey.description: Type key: lowercase Latin letters, digits, _ and -

jsonSchema.description: Document JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). The core rejects remote $ref.

requires.description: Packages whose objects this package refers to: a key (any version) or {package, version} with a SemVer range

engines.description: Version ranges of the components the package is tested against, e.g. {control-plane: ">=0.9,<0.11"}; check and plan reject an incompatible version before writing

variables.description: Declaration of every ${NAME} of the package. A used variable must be declared, a declared one must be used. There are no secrets in a package: a variable has no secret field

knowledge.description: Ontologies (name@major) the package's processes and rules rely on; check matches them against recall/remember/memory of the processes

renames.description: Explicit object renames (like moved in Terraform): the plan moves the object instead of deleting and creating it

packageSettings.description: Package settings: values an organization administrator changes in the live system without a new package version or an installation plan. Values live in the core; processes, work rules and views read them as settings.<field>

uischema.description: Form layout: the closed subset of JSON Forms the console renders — VerticalLayout, HorizontalLayout, Group, Control and Label with SHOW/HIDE/ENABLE/DISABLE rules; anything else, options of a Control included, is rejected. Labels are keys of the package dictionaries, not texts: label of a Group and of a Control, text of a Label. Unlike the uischema of process step forms, which is open and whose label is a text. Without it the console lays the fields out in schema order

settingsSchema.description: Schema of the settings: a subset of JSON Schema, as for process data. The root is an object; objects nest at most 3 levels deep; at most 100 properties per object. Field labels are not in the schema: they are keys <package>.settings.<path> of the package dictionaries

additionalProperties.description: Implied on every object: a value with an undeclared member is refused

settingsFieldName.description: Field name: camelCase, as referenced in expressions (settings.<field>)

settingsRequired.description: Fields that must always have a value

settingsKeywords.description: One settings field: only the keywords listed here; secret markers (writeOnly, format: password) and keywords outside the subset are rejected

default.description: Value in effect until an administrator saves another; every optional field must have one (package-sdk check)

x-ref.description: The string references a platform object of this kind in the organization: the id of a role, principal or workspace, the key of a task type or calendar; the core rejects a value that references a missing object

settingsField3.description: The deepest level: a scalar field or an array of scalars, no nested objects

settingsLabelKey.description: Key of the package dictionaries (<package>.settings.<name>), not the text: the console shows its string in the user's language

settingsScope.description: JSON Pointer to a property of the settings schema: #/properties/<field>[/properties/<field>…]

settingsUiRule.description: JSON Forms rule: the effect applies while the value at condition.scope matches condition.schema

schema.description: Condition on the value: the keywords of a settings field without x-ref and default, and const

settingsUiElement.description: Element of the settings form: VerticalLayout, HorizontalLayout, Group, Control or Label. Other JSON Forms elements (Categorization, ListWithDetail, custom renderers) are not rendered by the console and are rejected

scope.description: Property of the settings schema this control edits; package-sdk check resolves it against the schema

label.description: Dictionary key instead of the field's own <package>.settings.<path>

semverRange.description: Version range: comma-separated conditions, all must hold (>=0.9,<0.11); operators >=, >, <=, <, =, ^, ~; without an operator, a version or prefix (1.2 = 1.2.x); * means any

kind.description: Value kind: url is an absolute URL; workspace|project|principal|role is a UUID existing on the environment (checked by plan); integer is an integer; string is anything

default.description: Value used if the installation did not set its own

oneOf.description: Installation catalog package (packages/<key> next to the installation file or spec.packagesDir)

path.description: Package directory path relative to the installation file

git.description: https://host/path without credentials in the address, or git@host:path; access through the git credential helper

ref.description: Package release tag (refs/tags/<ref>; branches and commits are not accepted); packages.lock keeps it reproducible

path.description: Package subdirectory in the repository if it is not at the root: a relative path without . and ..

packages.description: Installation packages: a key (installation catalog), {key, path} or {key, git, ref}; requires are pulled in automatically. Empty means only the core's system task type

packagesDir.description: Installation packages directory relative to the installation file; defaults to packages/ next to it

knowledge.description: Ontology inclusion for work spaces is topology, hence in the installation; the set replaces the previous one entirely

strict.description: Strict memory mode: records outside the included kinds are rejected rather than accepted as is

retire.description: Keys the environment retires (all active versions → deprecated)

Agent.description: The agent is retired: the executor is stopped, the credential revoked, the history kept

NotificationRule.description: The notification rule is retired in the notification service (:retire); sent notifications remain

WorkRule.description: The work rule is archived; work it created lives on

Process.description: The process is retired via the core's :retire route: new instances do not start, live ones run to completion

Calendar.description: A calendar is retired only if no active process refers to it (calendar_in_use)

ConnectionType.description: Every active version of the connection type becomes deprecated: no new connections of the type, existing ones keep working

outcomeAction.description: One approval outcome action: an object with exactly one key. In strings, $.path expressions; the ! suffix makes the value required.

key.description: Idempotency key of the created work

customFields.description: Fields of the created task: expressions/templates; checked against the target type's fieldSchema at execution

requestApproval.description: Gate approval on the task just created

assignee.description: Principal id or role:<slug>, a role declared by the package (its holder decides); an expression or template

invokeSkill.description: Skill call; reactions run on the call's outcome

skill.description: name@version (required with a version for external_write)

expect.description: expected outputs fields; a mismatch triggers onFailure

gates.description: Only the default gate is supported for now

execution.description: A task of this type is executed by one skill call

inputs.description: $.… path to the whole input or an object {inputName: path}; defaults to $.customFields

completionSchema.description: Work after the task completes: {onComplete: {when?, actions}}: ensureWork (customFields, relation, requestApproval) and comment. The core checks the grammar.

instructions.description: Instructions for the executor: Markdown ≤ 16 KiB, the task type layer after the platform and project contract. The core checks the size in bytes and the absence of secrets.

executorRoles.description: Keys of the roles a person needs to take work of this type: a Role of the package, its requires or the tenant. Absent or empty — people are not restricted. The core refuses a role the tenant does not have (422 unknown_role).

acceptance.description: Default acceptance criteria for all tasks of the type: run after the required outputs and before the task's own criteria; a task cannot replace a type criterion, its criterion with the same key is rejected (422). deterministic with an external_write skill only after human in the same attempt.

contextSchema.description: Task context profile: anchors, traverse, asOf, budgetTokens. The core checks the grammar.

mediaType.description: Lowercase media type; a */* or type/* mask is allowed

artifactTypeSpec.description: Artifact type: a versioned immutable catalog object, like TaskType.

metadataSchema.description: Metadata schema of artifacts of this type (≤ 16 KiB)

mediaTypes.description: Allowed content media types; any by default

maxBytes.description: Content size limit; no more than the installation's global limit (CP_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES)

key.description: Input or output name; unique within inputs and within outputs

mediaTypes.description: Narrowing of the artifact type's media types (a subset of its mediaTypes)

artifactSchema.description: Task type inputs and outputs. An input is the head revisions of artifacts of the required type on tasks via a relation; without a required input, claim is rejected (409 input_missing). A required output is a deterministic criterion of the verification stage.

from.description: Relation used to find the source task

content.description: Whether the content must be in storage (otherwise a reference is enough)

workRuleSpec.description: Work rule: exactly the POST /rules body without key. The core checks the grammar of conditions and templates (normalize_rule_spec). workspaceId is installation topology: only via a ${VARIABLE}, set on creation and not changed afterwards.

agent.description: Only with observation: the observation matches when its author is the principal of this agent. An agent key or an installation ${VARIABLE} — a neutral package does not know the provider's agent

taskType.description: Type key or a {{item.…}} template; a template only with non-empty taskTypes

taskTypes.description: Allowed types for a templated taskType; with complete_work and cancel_work with target: task — the types the rule may close

target.description: Only with complete_work and cancel_work: dedup — the work under the rule's key (the default), task — the task the triggering observation is bound to; needs taskTypes and an author filter trigger.agent or trigger.actorId

workspaceId.description: Template of the workspace id of the created work; defaults to the rule's workspace

relations.description: Relations of the created work: spawnedBy is a task id template; dependsOn are deduplication keys of this rule's work (from the same evaluation or created earlier)

identity.description: On whose behalf the rule acts: an agent description of kind service or agent; without identity, with the authority of whoever applied the rule

notificationRuleSpec.description: Notification rule: core event and condition → recipient → text and buttons. Stored and executed by the notification service; templates are {{payload.…}}, {{event.…}}, {{task.…}} substitution without logic.

type.description: Core catalog event type or a prefix.*

when.description: Condition in the core rule grammar over payload, event and task

ref.description: Path to a principal or role in the event (assigned, role) or an id/variable (principal)

workspace.description: Path to the workspace for role; defaults to the event's workspace

type.description: Notification type: recipient settings and mandatory rules work by it

actions.description: approvalDecide: Approve/Reject buttons for the decision from payload.approvalId

close.description: Close the notification's buttons with the same deduplication key when the event arrives

outcome.description: Outcome template shown instead of the buttons

cel.description: CEL expression in the taimen/1 profile: variables data, event, step, task, instance; cal.* functions; no current time. The core checks types and the cost limit

processElementId.description: Stable process element id: the schema layout, migration maps, the journal and the memory graph refer to it. Renaming only via the migrations map

durationOrCel.description: ISO 8601 duration or a CEL expression yielding a point in time (timestamp) or a duration

workdayCount.description: Workdays by the calendar: the same time of day n workdays later (cal.addWorkdays)

workhourCount.description: Working-time hours by a calendar with working hours (cal.addWorkingTime)

workingAmountExpr.description: Number of work units as a CEL expression: a non-negative integer, evaluated once on entering the step (settings.* are the package settings); after that the due date is computed as from a number

workingSpan.description: Interval: an ISO 8601 duration (astronomical time), {workdays} or {workhours} by the due calendar

processDue.description: Due (SLA) of a step or process: an ISO 8601 duration, {at}, a point in time or a duration from data, or exactly one of duration, workdays, workhours with optional calendar and warnBefore

calendar.description: Calendar of the working units; defaults to the process's spec.calendar

warnBefore.description: Warning threshold before the due; without it there is no warning

celMap.description: Path in the instance data → CEL expression

processTrigger.description: Event source: a core journal event or an observation. where is a CEL filter over event

governedBy.description: Knowledge base regulations the element is subject to: the natural key of the memory document and, if needed, a clause

expr.description: CEL → principal id, agent:<key> or role:<slug>

assignChain.description: Candidates in order: the first resolvable one is taken

memoryAnchor.description: Graph traversal anchor: the instance's case node or an entity by natural key (CEL over data)

memoryTraverse.description: Traversal steps from the anchors, the same shape as traverse in contextSchema

memoryWhere.description: Filters on node attributes: applied to result nodes and to candidate anchors of semantic expansion; conditions are joined with AND

attr.description: Node attribute name (flat), e.g. okpd2 or validUntil; a list attribute satisfies the condition if any of its elements does

op.description: prefix compares codes by dot-separated segments: 62.01 matches 62.01.11 but not 62.011; lte/gte are RFC 3339 dates or numbers

value.description: CEL expression over the instance data (a string literal goes in CEL quotes: "'62.01'"); for in, a CEL list or a list of expressions; for exists, true or false

stepContext.description: Context profile of the step executor from memory: explicit relations first, semantic expansion marked inferred

after.description: due means at the due moment; a duration means after the due

processForm.description: Step form: JSON Schema of the data and JSON Forms uischema of the view

processStep.description: Process step: exactly one kind (human, approve, call, decide, recall, remember, listen, wait, set, raise, compensate, fork, try, do, suspend, resume, complete) plus common fields

when.description: Guard: the step runs only if it is true

output.description: Writing the step result (step.result) into the instance data

onCompensate.description: Compensation of a completed step: runs on compensate in reverse order

customFields.description: Prefill of the created task's fields with case data: a field of the type's fieldSchema → CEL; checked against fieldSchema on publication and on task creation, null leaves the field to the human

separationOfDuties.description: CEL → list of principals who may not vote; the core checks it at decision time

recall.description: Memory query through the core; the answer is a journal event (deterministic replay)

remember.description: Write to memory as a core observation from the process identity, with a reference to the case

listen.description: Waiting for the first of the events (deferred choice); timeout is a timer

wait.description: Pause: a duration or a point in time; wait has no due, the pause itself sets the time

compensate.description: Run onCompensate of completed steps in reverse order

on.description: Error types to retry; all by default

processStage.description: Case stage (CMMN): entry and exit by guards, milestones, required and optional work

entry.description: Entry guard; stage.<id>.completed, milestone.<id> and data are available in the expression

discretionary.description: Work a human adds at their discretion

processTimers.description: Boundary timers: fire while the stage (process) is open; at from data is recalculated when the data changes

decisionTable.description: Decision table (DMN in spirit). Condition cell: '-' (any), a literal, a list 'a,b', a range '[a..b)'

memoryProjection.description: Projection of the case into the memory graph: delivered by events, only declared fields go into the graph

facts.description: Case fact name → value; a change closes the previous fact with a validity end

many.description: key yields a list: one entity per element

processSpec.description: Process: a case with stages and execution blocks, data by schema, CEL expressions, projection into memory. Executed by the core

version.description: Definition version: a published version is immutable

identity.description: On whose behalf the process acts: an agent description of kind service or agent

owner.description: Process owner: tasks about the process are addressed to them (divergence from the regulation, instance errors). Optional; the package check warns if it is missing

due.description: Due of the whole process from the instance start

data.description: JSON Schema of the instance data; package-sdk expands {$ref: <package file>}

key.description: Instance key: a repeated event with the same key is a correlate, not a new instance

retrospective.description: Review of a closed case: the agent proposes lessons, a human confirms

appliesTo.description: Entity kinds lessons are attached to

workingIntervals.description: Working-time intervals of the day, in order and non-overlapping, from before to (the core checks the order); 24:00 is the end of the day

calendarSpec.description: Business calendar: default days off, holidays and transfers by year

workingHours.description: Working hours on the calendar's working days, in the calendar's local time. Without the field the calendar knows only working days

intervals.description: Intervals of a regular working day

weekdays.description: Intervals per ISO weekday (1 is Monday) instead of intervals; [] means no working hours

shortDayReduction.description: How much shorter a shortened day (shortDays) is: subtracted from the end of the last interval

provisional.description: The year is not approved yet: cal.* results are marked as preliminary

workdays.description: Transferred working days that fall on days off

connectionKey.description: Key of a connection type or of a connection

connectionTypeSpec.description: Connection type: what it takes to connect a system of this kind. Versions work as for Skill: the package sets the version, and a published (key, version) pair is immutable. A type carries no secret values: an administrator enters them in the console.

version.description: The package sets the version of the type; a published version is immutable

auth.description: Ways to connect: oauth2 — a person consents at the provider, token — a long-lived key an administrator pastes

authorizeUrl.description: Where a person is sent to consent

tokenUrlTemplate.description: Address of the code exchange and refresh; the only placeholder is {account}, the host is an external DNS name

accountParam.description: Callback parameter that names the account; required when tokenUrlTemplate has {account}

authStyle.description: How the client id and secret go to the exchange address: in the request body or as Authorization: Basic

accountField.description: Account field: its label in the key form and the account check; required with token or with {account} in tokenUrlTemplate

pattern.description: Regular expression the whole account matches

settingsSchema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the connection's non-secret settings, root type: object. Properties named like secrets (password, token, clientSecret…) are refused

defaultKey.description: Key of the default connection — the agents of the package name it in Agent.spec.connections

skillContract.description: Skill v1 contract. Immutable within a version.

version.description: The package sets the skill version
